## Folk sources [Record]

*Aušrinė* is the morning star (Venus), in the mythological *daina* of the Moon's marriage the one for whom [Mėnuo](menuo.qmd) leaves [Saulė](saule.qmd); [Perkūnas](perkunas.qmd) cuts the Moon in two for it ([legends §7](../codex/legends-songs.qmd)). Old women say she was a child, village girls say she was a thief; she is never punished. Several variants make her Saulė's or Dievas's daughter.

## In the saga

A figure of folk myth only: no domain, no element, no Force-face. She is the unpunished seducer of the saga's law (the oath-breaker is cut, the seducer goes free), which Book II can use as a theme. The graph links her to Mėnuo as the folk tale's third party.

## Offerings & taboos

No cult or offering is recorded.

## Pronunciation

**OW-shree-neh** (stress *AUŠ-ri-nė*).
